title: Redescription of the marbled stargazer Uranoscopus marmoratus Cuvier, 1829 (Labriformes, Uranoscopidae)
content:
Abstract

The Marbled Stargazer, Uranoscopus marmoratus, is redescribed based on five individuals collected from the southeastern Arabian Sea, India. This species is a poorly known fish which is distributed predominantly in the eastern Indian Ocean and belongs to the Uranoscopus japonicus species group. U. marmoratus is defined as having one pair of basipterygial processes; a simple posterior nostril and tubular anterior nostril; one internal supracleithral spine and one sharp humeral spine; 4–5 preopercular and 1 subopercular spines; no scales on the predorsal region; no supraocular cirri; 52–62 transverse rows of scales on the sides of the body; well-developed occipital lobes; occipital commissure with four posterior branches; head length 2.6–3.6 times in standard length; head large; head width 3.0–3.3 times in standard length; body depth 4.2–4.7 times in standard length; head depth 1.1–1.4 times its width; dorsal surface marbled, with pale spots on a brown background. Otolith morphological description of the fish was also provided for the first time. COI sequence generated herein represents the first genetic record of the species in GenBank, and Maximum-Likelihood (K2P) analysis recovered this species as a distinct lineage, offering additional support for its taxonomic distinctiveness.
